title: frontend: profile and speed up the jest suite, shard it under bazel (2.2x)
body:
## Summary

This PR speeds up the Bazel Jest target by using a transpile-only `ts-jest` transform and partitioning it into four Bazel-owned shards. The original profiling identified repeated per-file TypeScript program construction as the dominant cost; the transform avoids that duplicate work while CI's Frontend Build and Test step still type-checks all of `src`, including test files.

The branch is rebased onto current `main`. It preserves main's `jest.setup.cjs` TextEncoder/TextDecoder polyfill in both Jest configuration and Bazel runfiles, so React Router remains loadable in jsdom.

- Adds a conditional shard sequencer for Bazel's runtime shard environment and retains Jest's default sequencer for bare local runs.
- Keeps Jest in-band within each Bazel shard; Bazel owns the four-way parallelism.
- Stores Bazel-run Jest cache data under `TEST_TMPDIR`, avoiding host temporary-directory accumulation while retaining Jest's default cache location for bare runs.
- Covers failed-test selection so an already-sharded list is ordered but never partitioned a second time.

## Measurements

The rebased target now runs 58 suites and 449 tests. The current four shards contain 15/15/14/14 suites and 107/160/93/89 tests, respectively, for an exact 449-test partition.

Worker configuration was measured by alternating the shipped in-band configuration with `--maxWorkers=4` after removing `--runInBand`. On this machine, in-band Bazel shards completed in 39.6–43.3s; allowing four Jest workers inside every shard took 97.9–102.4s. The latter oversubscribes the four concurrently scheduled Bazel shards, so this PR deliberately keeps `--runInBand`.

## Scope

Jest-level sharding for local `npm test` runs remains explicitly out of scope; Jest already supports `--shard=N/M` for that separate workflow.

## Verification

- `bazel build //frontend:jest_test`
- `bazel test //frontend:jest_test --test_output=errors`
- `checkleft run`

@@ -55,4 +56,9 @@ bin.jest_test(
         "public/**",
         "src/**/*.json",
     ]),
+    # Bazel hands each shard TEST_TOTAL_SHARDS/TEST_SHARD_INDEX, which
+    # jest.shard-sequencer.cjs turns into a partition of the test files.
+    # Each shard is a single in-band jest process, so Bazel (not jest)
+    # owns the parallelism and the shards cannot oversubscribe each other.
+    shard_count = 4,
 )

before.content:
load("@npm//:defs.bzl", "npm_link_all_packages")
load("@npm//frontend:jest/package_json.bzl", "bin")

npm_link_all_packages(name = "node_modules")

JS_TEST_FILES = glob(
    [
        "**/*.test.js",
        "**/*.test.jsx",
        "**/*.test.ts",
        "**/*.test.tsx",
        "**/*.spec.js",
        "**/*.spec.jsx",
        "**/*.spec.ts",
        "**/*.spec.tsx",
    ],
    allow_empty = True,
    exclude = [
        "dist/**",
        "node_modules/**",
    ],
)

FRONTEND_JS_TS_FILES = glob(
    [
        "**/*.js",
        "**/*.jsx",
        "**/*.ts",
        "**/*.tsx",
    ],
    allow_empty = True,
    exclude = [
        "dist/**",
        "node_modules/**",
    ],
)

bin.jest_test(
    name = "jest_test",
    args = [
        "--ci",
        "--config",
        "$(rootpath :jest.config.cjs)",
        "--runInBand",
        "--runTestsByPath",
    ] + ["$(rootpath {})".format(test_file) for test_file in JS_TEST_FILES],
    data = [
        "jest.config.cjs",
        "jest.setup.cjs",
        "package.json",
        "tsconfig.json",
        "tsconfig.node.json",
        ":node_modules",
    ] + FRONTEND_JS_TS_FILES + glob([
        "public/**",
        "src/**/*.json",
    ]),
)

files.patch:
@@ -1,7 +1,34 @@
 /** @type {import('ts-jest').JestConfigWithTsJest} */
 module.exports = {
-  preset: "ts-jest",
   testEnvironment: "jsdom",
+  // Only installed when Bazel asks for sharding; bare `npx jest` and
+  // unsharded runs keep jest's default sequencer. See the sequencer file.
+  ...(process.env.TEST_TOTAL_SHARDS ? { testSequencer: "<rootDir>/jest.shard-sequencer.cjs" } : {}),
   moduleFileExtensions: ["ts", "tsx", "js", "jsx", "json", "node"],
   setupFiles: ["<rootDir>/jest.setup.cjs"],
+  transform: {
+    // Transpile-only. Type checking is NOT done here. CI always runs `tsc`
+    // over all of `src` (test files included) in the Frontend Build and Test
+    // step, which is gated on the same frontend-changed condition as this
+    // target, so type errors in test files still fail the build. Doing it
+    // again per jest worker is duplicate work. tsconfig.json already sets
+    // `isolatedModules: true`, so the codebase is required to be safe to
+    // transpile file-by-file.
+    "^.+\\.[tj]sx?$": [
+      "ts-jest",
+      {
+        isolatedModules: true,
+        // Jest's runtime is CommonJS, but the app tsconfig targets an ESM
+        // bundler. Override just enough for the module system to line up;
+        // everything else (jsx, jsxImportSource, target, lib) is inherited
+        // from tsconfig.json.
+        tsconfig: {
+          module: "CommonJS",
+          moduleResolution: "Node",
+          esModuleInterop: true,
+        },
+      },
+    ],
+  },
+  ...(process.env.TEST_TMPDIR ? { cacheDirectory: `${process.env.TEST_TMPDIR}/jest-cache` } : {}),
 };
